newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MOENCHENGLADBACH LOOK BACK IN HOPE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MOENCHENGLADBACH LOOK BACK IN HOPE.

text.p: Struggling Borussia Moenchengladbach have decided to turn their minds back to a rare bright day in their dismal first half of the season before they visit German league leaders Borussia Dortmund on Saturday.

Moenchengladbach have wanted to forget most of their matches before the winter break when they slipped down and down the Bundesliga --- apart from a wonderful day in September when they fired five goals past Dortmund in the western German derby.

The reigning champions were outplayed that day in the clash of the two Borussias. But now former UEFA Cup winners Moenchengladbach are struggling down in 13th in the league before the clash in Dortmund's intimidating Westfalen stadium.
"We must put that game into our minds on Saturday," Moenchengladbach's versatile midfielder Martin Schneider said.

Dortmund, who lead the table on goal difference from Bayern Munich, are on a high after beating France's Auxerre in midweek to clinch a place in the European Cup semifinals where they will meet England's Manchester United next month.
The champions' biggest problem is consistency, however. Last week they were taken apart by VfB Stuttgart in a 4-1 defeat but still bounced back to win 1-0 in Auxerre.
Saturday's game could be tight, however, despite the two teams' contrasting positions in the table.
"We are still missing consistent form. There are too many highs and lows," the club's experienced defender Juergen Kohler said. "We have to deal with that."
Moenchengladbach are a lot better side than their lowly position suggests. With their former international midfielder Stefan Effenberg returning to his best, they are playing well again.
The statistics are against them, however. Dortmund, who are chasing a third consecutive title, have not lost at home this season while Moenchengladbach have won just one of 12 games away from home.

Dortmund chairman Gerd Niebaum was quick to point out to the team that they should not get too carried away by the success in Europe. They are unlikely to lack concentration with such a tight situation in the Bundesliga.
Just two points separate the top four -- Dortmund, Bayern, Stuttgart and Bayer Leverkusen.
"After going through in Europe we are going to have more problems defending our title," Niebaum said. "If we had gone out the chances of getting the third title would have been better.
"I want to win the championship again. That is our task. The European Cup is a Sunday afternoon out."
Dortmund were trying to rest their legs after the European tie before seeing who is carrying injuries before Saturday.
Moenchengladbach will definitely be without Romanian midfielder Ioan Lupescu who is suspended but the in-form Schneider should be able to step into his defensive midfield role.

Borussia Dortmund - 1-Stefan Klos, 6-Matthias Sammer, 15-Juergen Kohler, 17-Joerg Heinrich, 19-Paulo Sousa, 14-Paul Lambert, 18-Lars Ricken, 7-Stefan Reuter, 10-Andy Moeller, 9-Stephane Chapuisat, 13-Karlheinz Riedle.

Moenchengladbach - 1-Uwe Kamps, 27-Stephan Passlack, 4-Patrik Andersson, 21-Hubert Fournier, 6-Joerg Neun, 13-Martin Schneider, 10-Stefan Effenberg, 7-Karlheinz Pflipsen, 8-Peter Wynhoff, 9-Andrzej Juskoviak, 30-Martin Dahlin.
